titulo: Estar para + infinitive = to be ready / about to; no estar para = not in the mood
subtitulo: Estoy para dormirme. No estoy para bromas.
regla: Estar para + infinitive = to be ready for or about to: los duraznos están para comerse. No estar para + infinitive / noun = not to be in the mood or condition for: No estoy para bromas.

lista.texto: _ready for, about to_: **ya está para casarse**, **está para llover**.
_not in the mood / condition for_: **no estoy para bromas**, **no estoy para caminar mucho**.

bloques.texto: **Está para llover** = **está por llover** (_it's about to rain_); in Mexico **por** is more common for _about to_.
Tip: **no estoy para...** = don't push it today.

lista.en: My daughter is ready to get married.
The peaches are ripe and ready to eat.

lista.es: Tuve un día larguísimo. ==Estoy para== acostarme.
lista.en: I had a really long day. I'm ready for bed.

lista.es: ==No estoy para== caminar mucho; todavía me duele la rodilla.
lista.en: I'm in no shape to walk much; my knee still hurts.

lista.es: Miguel ==no está para== bromas. Hoy se peleó con su jefe.
lista.en: Miguel isn't in the mood for jokes. He fought with his boss today.
I'm not available to anyone. (don't bother me)

lista.nota: **Estar para** = ready / in the mood, not purpose.

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _I'm not in the mood for parties._
In Spanish: _The bread is ready to come out of the oven._
lista.r: El pan está para sacarse del horno.

lista.p: In Spanish: _I'm in no condition to drive._
